ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, the plane of the coil makes an angle $\theta{=}60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal direction, the magnetic field lines are vertically downward, the area of the coil plane is $S{=}0.4\mathrm{m}^{2}$, and the magnetic induction intensity of the uniform magnetic field is $B{=}0.6\mathrm{T}$.

1. What is the magnetic flux $\varPhi$ passing through the coil?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the plane of the coil makes an angle $\theta{=}60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal direction, the magnetic field lines are vertically downward, the area of the coil plane is $S{=}0.4\mathrm{m}^{2}$, and the magnetic induction intensity of the uniform magnetic field is $B{=}0.6\mathrm{T}$. 1. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the coil is drawn as an inclined parallelogram, with dashed lines around it indicating its horizontal projection or auxiliary lines; multiple magnetic field line arrows are vertically downward; below the parallelogram near side d, θ is used to mark the inclination angle of the coil plane relative to the horizontal reference direction. The problem statement gives θ = 60°, the coil area S = 0.4 m², and the magnetic induction intensity of the uniform magnetic field B = 0.6 T. Reasoning: The magnetic flux is calculated according to the direction of the coil area vector, with the formula Φ = B S cos α, where α is the angle between the magnetic field direction and the normal to the coil plane. The coil plane makes θ = 60° with the horizontal plane, and the magnetic field is vertically downward, so the angle between the normal to the coil plane and the vertical magnetic field direction can be taken as α = θ = 60°. Substituting gives Φ = 0.6 × 0.4 × cos60° = 0.6 × 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.12 Wb.
